_about: Public-domain John Henry Augustus Bomberger (1817-1890), German Reformed pastor, first president of Ursinus College and leading critic of the Mercersburg theology, for the Word Hoard: Spiritual Libertinism (1846), Infant Salvation (1859), Five Years' Ministry in Race Street (1860) and Reformed, not Ritualistic (1867), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 56 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

bomberger-spiritual-libertinism: Spiritual libertinism : an address delivered before the alumni association of Marshall College, September 8th, 1846 / by J.H.A. Bomberger (Printed at the Office of the Ger. Reformed Church, 1846)
bomberger-infant-salvation: Infant salvation : in its relation to infant depravity, infant regeneration, and infant baptism (Philadelphia : Lindsay & Blakiston, 1859)
bomberger-five-years: Five Years' Ministry in the German Reformed Church, in Race Street, Below Fourth, Philadelphia (Lindsay & Blakiston, 1860)
bomberger-reformed-not-ritualistic: Reformed, not ritualistic : Apostolic, not patristic : a reply to Dr. Nevin's Vindication, etc (Philadelphia : [s.n.], 1867)

_excluded.bomberger-other: His condensed translation of Herzog's Protestant Theological Encyclopedia (1858-60, a translation of a multi-author work); Kurtz's Text-book of Church History (another author); Three Thousand Practical Illustrations (1909 compilation)

PHILADELPHIA: LINDSAY & BLAKISTON. 1860' (Bomberger garbled); the consistory's letter is addressed to him as pastor of the Race Street German Reformed Church.
